body_es:
Un sistema tolerante a fallos sigue funcionando correctamente (o de forma degradada) cuando algunos de sus componentes fallan. Los fallos son inevitables en sistemas distribuidos: los discos fallan, las redes se saturan, los procesos se bloquean.

Las técnicas principales son: redundancia (componentes duplicados para que el fallo de uno no detenga el sistema), replicación de datos (copias en múltiples nodos), failover automático (detección de fallo y conmutación automática a un componente de respaldo), bulkheads (aislar partes del sistema para que el fallo de una no afecte a las demás) y timeouts con fallback (si un servicio no responde en N milisegundos, usar un valor por defecto o un servicio alternativo).

Las métricas de confiabilidad son MTBF (Mean Time Between Failures, tiempo medio entre fallos) y MTTR (Mean Time To Recovery, tiempo medio de recuperación). Un sistema de alta disponibilidad maximiza MTBF y minimiza MTTR.

El patrón de degración elegante (graceful degradation) es esencial: cuando el sistema de recomendaciones falla, el e-commerce sigue funcionando sin recomendaciones, en lugar de mostrar un error completo. La funcionalidad crítica sigue disponible mientras la funcionalidad secundaria se deshabilita.
body_en:
A fault-tolerant system continues to operate correctly—or in a gracefully degraded mode—when some of its components fail. In distributed systems, failures are not the exception; they are the expected operating condition.

Core techniques include: redundancy (duplicate components so one failure does not stop the system), data replication (copies on multiple nodes), automatic failover (detect failure and switch to a standby component without human intervention), bulkheads (isolate system parts so a failure in one cannot cascade to others), and timeouts with fallbacks (if a service does not respond within N milliseconds, use a cached value or default response rather than blocking indefinitely).

Reliability is measured by MTBF (Mean Time Between Failures) and MTTR (Mean Time To Recovery). High availability maximises MTBF and minimises MTTR.

Graceful degradation is the key design principle: when the recommendation engine fails, the e-commerce site still sells products—it just shows no recommendations. Critical paths stay up; non-critical features degrade silently.
example_code:
# Fault-tolerant service call with timeout + fallback
import time

def call_recommendation_service(user_id, timeout_ms=100):
    """Simulates a sometimes-slow recommendation service."""
    start = time.monotonic()
    # Simulate service latency based on user_id (odd = slow, even = fast)
    simulated_latency_ms = 200 if user_id % 2 != 0 else 50
    elapsed_ms = (time.monotonic() - start) * 1000
    if simulated_latency_ms > timeout_ms:
        raise TimeoutError(f'Recommendation service timed out ({simulated_latency_ms}ms)')
    return [f'product-{user_id * 10 + i}' for i in range(3)]

def get_recommendations(user_id):
    try:
        recs = call_recommendation_service(user_id)
        print(f'[OK]      user {user_id}: {recs}')
        return recs
    except TimeoutError as e:
        print(f'[FALLBACK] user {user_id}: {e}')
        return ['bestseller-1', 'bestseller-2']  # graceful degradation

for uid in [2, 3, 4, 7]:
    get_recommendations(uid)
